meta.name: Puli First Year Costs
meta.excerpt: The Puli's main ownership cost is time rather than money — cord management is labor-intensive but inexpensive. This guide covers first-year expenses and what to budget for this athletic Hungarian herding breed.
meta.meta_description: Puli first year costs: puppy price, food, vet care, and annual budget for Hungary's iconic corded herding breed.

intro.label: Upfront Costs
intro.heading: Moderate Puppy Cost for a Rare Breed
intro.html:
• Puppy from health-tested breeder: $1,200–$2,000. Health testing should include OFA hip evaluation and CAER eye certification.
  • Initial vet visit and vaccines: $150–$350
  • Spay or neuter: $250–$500
  • Crate (large): $70–$150
  • Bowls, collar, harness, leash, ID tag: $70–$150
  • Medium-breed puppy food (first months): $70–$140
  • Puppy classes: $100–$200
  • High-velocity dryer (essential for bathing a corded dog): $80–$200 — this is a Puli-specific investment that pays for itself in reduced professional grooming needs

Upfront total estimate: $1,990–$3,690

care.label: First Year Recurring
care.heading: The Main Cost Is Time, Not Money
care.html:
The Puli's cord management is labor-intensive but not expensive — it requires your hands and time, not specialized products. The main monetary costs are food, routine veterinary care, and the investment in a quality high-velocity dryer for bathing.

  • Food (medium-breed active formula): $60–$90/month. Annual: $720–$1,080.
  • Routine vet visits and vaccines: $250–$450
  • Heartworm/parasite prevention: $90–$180/year
  • Pet insurance: $30–$55/month. Annual: $360–$660.
  • Grooming products (gentle shampoo, conditioner): $50–$100/year
  • Toys, enrichment: $80–$180/year

First-year recurring total (with insurance): $1,550–$2,650

special.label: Total & Ongoing
special.heading: Year One and Annual Budget
special.html:
Total first-year estimate (with insurance): $3,540–$6,340

Annual ongoing costs after year one:

  • Food: $720–$1,080
  • Routine vet care: $200–$400
  • Parasite prevention: $90–$180
  • Pet insurance: $360–$720
  • Grooming products: $50–$100
  • Miscellaneous: $100–$200

Estimated annual ongoing total: $1,520–$2,680

Note on the brushed coat option: Owners who maintain the Puli in a brushed (non-corded) coat have essentially the same ongoing costs — there is no significant monetary difference. The difference is in the type of time investment: cord separation vs. regular brushing.

faq.q: Is the Puli expensive to groom professionally?
faq.a: Professional groomers experienced with corded coats are rare and charge accordingly when found. Most Puli owners learn to manage the cords themselves. The main investment is a quality high-velocity dryer ($80–$200) that makes home bathing of the corded coat much more practical.

faq.q: What is the biggest time commitment in Puli ownership?
faq.a: During the cord formation period (9 months to 2 years), cord separation 2–3 times per week is the primary time commitment. Once cords are established, bath days become the main time investment — allowing 6–12 hours for drying a fully corded adult dog.

faq.q: Is the Puli an expensive breed to own overall?
faq.a: Relative to its size, the Puli is not an expensive breed monetarily. The main cost is time. Annual monetary costs are comparable to other medium-sized active breeds — the cord management and long bathing sessions are the real commitment.
